prompt:
Score each of the items below on each of these features:
- dominant_blue (scale): How much of the creature's body is blue/cyan colored. 0=no blue at all, 1=almost entirely blue
- dominant_green (scale): How much of the creature's body is green colored. 0=no green, 1=almost entirely green
- dominant_brown (scale): How much of the creature's body is brown/tan colored. 0=no brown, 1=almost entirely brown
- dominant_red_pink (scale): How much of the creature's body is red, pink, or magenta. 0=none, 1=almost entirely red/pink
- dominant_yellow_orange (scale): How much of the creature's body is yellow or orange. 0=none, 1=almost entirely yellow/orange
- dominant_gray_black (scale): How much of the creature's body is gray, black, or dark metallic. 0=none, 1=almost entirely gray/black
- dominant_white (scale): How much of the creature's body is white or very pale. 0=none, 1=almost entirely white
- has_wings (binary): Whether the creature has visible wings or wing-like appendages
- has_fins_or_tail_fin (binary): Whether the creature has aquatic fins or a fish-like tail
- has_tentacles (binary): Whether the creature has tentacles or tentacle-like appendages
- bipedal (binary): Whether the creature stands upright on two legs
- quadruped (binary): Whether the creature stands on four legs
- amorphous_blob (scale): Whether the creature lacks clear limbs and has a blob-like or spherical body. 0=clear limbed body, 1=completely amorphous/round
- body_complexity (scale): Visual complexity of the design: number of appendages, patterns, details. 0=very simple/smooth, 1=extremely complex with many details
- apparent_size (scale): How large/bulky the creature appears to be. 0=tiny/small, 1=very large/massive
- fierceness (scale): How fierce, aggressive, or intimidating the creature looks. 0=cute/gentle, 1=very fierce/menacing
- cuteness (scale): How cute or adorable the creature appears. 0=not cute at all, 1=extremely cute
- insectoid (binary): Whether the creature resembles an insect or arachnid (exoskeleton, multiple limbs, pincers)
- aquatic_body (scale): Whether the creature has a body adapted for water (streamlined, fish-like, marine). 0=fully terrestrial, 1=fully aquatic
- avian (binary): Whether the creature is bird-like (beak, feathers, bird body plan)
- mammalian (binary): Whether the creature resembles a mammal (fur, mammalian face, warm-blooded appearance)
- reptilian (binary): Whether the creature resembles a reptile or dinosaur (scales, reptilian features)
- plant_features (binary): Whether the creature has plant-like features (leaves, petals, vines, roots)
- mechanical_mineral (scale): Whether the creature appears mechanical, rocky, or mineral-based rather than organic. 0=fully organic, 1=fully mechanical/mineral
- shell_or_armor (binary): Whether the creature has a visible shell, exoskeleton, or armor plating
- spiky_horns (binary): Whether the creature has prominent spikes, horns, or pointed protrusions
- floating_flying (scale): Whether the creature appears to be airborne or floating rather than grounded. 0=grounded, 1=fully airborne
- number_of_colors (scale): How many distinct major colors appear on the creature. 0=monochromatic (1 color), 1=very colorful (5+ colors)

Judge each item on its own. Scale features take a number from 0 to 1; binary features take 0 or 1.
Reply with JSON of the form:
{"rows": [{"item": "<item id>", "scores": {"<feature id>": <number>, ...}}, ...]}
with one row for every one of the 20 items and a score for every feature.

You can only change the feature set. You cannot set any individual item's scores: any new feature is scored for every item by an independent scorer that sees only your definition and the item.
Allowed changes:
- "weights": new weights (0 to 5) for existing features; 0 effectively turns a feature off
- "drop": ids of features to remove
- "add": up to 5 new features (new, unused ids). Each feature must be judgeable for ANY single item on its own, from what is shown for that item, without comparing to other items. kind is "scale" (a score from 0 to 1, define what 0 and 1 mean) or "binary" (0 or 1). - modern_design_style (scale): Whether the creature has a modern, sleek, detailed art style typical of newer Pokemon generations (Gen 5+) with sharper lines, more dynamic poses, and complex color gradients. 0=classic simple rounded style, 1=very modern sharp detailed style
- angular_geometric (scale): How angular or geometric the creature's body shape is, with sharp edges, pointed features, and non-organic shapes. 0=completely round and organic, 1=very angular and geometric
- dark_or_edgy_aesthetic (scale): Whether the creature has a dark, edgy, or cool aesthetic with dark color accents, sharp eyes, or menacing design elements. 0=bright, cheerful, innocent look, 1=dark, edgy, cool aesthetic
- multiple_body_segments (scale): Whether the creature's body is composed of multiple distinct segments, parts, or sections rather than one unified form. 0=single unified body, 1=many distinct segments or parts
- face_expression_intensity (scale): How intense or dramatic the creature's facial expression is. 0=blank, neutral, or minimal expression, 1=very intense, dramatic expression (angry, excited, determined)

Judge each item on its own. Scale features take a number from 0 to 1; binary features take 0 or 1.
Reply with JSON of the form:
{"rows": [{"item": "<item id>", "scores": {"<feature id>": <number>, ...}}, ...]}
with one row for every one of the 20 items and a score for every feature.
